LESSON: PROPERTIES OF MATTER

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
Strand: Matter
Topic 2.1: Properties of Matter

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Properties of Matter. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What are the properties of matter?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe the properties of the three states of matter
2. appreciate the importance of the different states of matter in day-to-day life
3. classify solid waste into decomposable and non- decomposable
4. describe the dangers of solid waste to the environment
5. apply appropriate methods to manage solid waste in the environment
6. appreciate the need for proper management of solid waste in the

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: PROPERTIES OF MATTER
Subject: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Properties of Matter helps you succeed in SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: PROPERTIES OF MATTER
Properties of Matter is part of Science learning. Connect every idea to something you can observe.
Use safe examples only. Do not try dangerous experiments without a teacher.
Write definitions in your own words, then add one drawing or real-life example.

PART 1: Describe the properties of the three states of matter

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the properties of the three states of matter. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the properties of the three states of matter.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Properties of Matter” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the properties of the three states of matter. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Properties of Matter is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Properties of Matter” around your school. (skill: describe the properties of the three states of matter)

Example 2: Say why Properties of Matter matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: appreciate the importance of the different states of matter in day-to-day life)

Example 3: Describe one safe action you can take related to Properties of Matter this week. (skill: classify solid waste into decomposable and non- decomposable)

Example 4: Name what you can see/touch about “Properties of Matter” around your school. (skill: describe the dangers of solid waste to the environment)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Properties of Matter to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe the properties of the three states of matter.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate the importance of the different states of matter in day-to-day life.
4. Practise this skill: classify solid waste into decomposable and non- decomposable.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Properties of Matter from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Properties of Matter: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Properties of Matter?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What are the properties of matter?
2. How is solid waste dangerous to the environment?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Properties of Matter means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe the properties of the three states of matter.
5. Be able to: appreciate the importance of the different states of matter in day-to-day life.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
